title: Cannot eject a non-mounted CD/DVD/BD via "Disks & Devices" applet
line: A CD, DVD or Blu-ray that isn't mounted can now be ejected from Disks & Devices: its action list has an Eject entry.
explanation: For an optical disc, Disks & Devices only offered Eject as the default action once the disc was mounted. An inserted but unmounted disc showed Mount and Open, and its expanded list only had Mount, so there was no way to eject it from the applet. The change adds an Eject action (new EjectAction, ejecting the disc's OpticalDrive) to the device's action list while an optical disc isn't mounted; when it is mounted, the default action already ejects it, so the entry hides.

commits.message:
applets/devicenotifier: offer Eject for optical discs that aren't mounted

An optical disc only offered Eject while it was mounted, so a disc that
was inserted but never mounted could not be ejected from the applet. Add
an Eject action to the disc's action list while it isn't mounted.

BUG: 469706

media.caption: Unmounted data disc, actions expanded: only Mount, no way to eject
Same disc with the fix: Eject is listed under Mount

review.text: Adds a dedicated EjectAction to Disks & Devices that appears in an optical disc's expanded action list while unmounted and hides once mounted (when the default action already ejects). Rightly avoids altering UnmountAction, which only drives the header's unmount-all button. The C++ implementation and CMake wiring are clean, and the UDisks2 mock verification covers both unmounted and mounted optical discs without duplicates.

reviews.text: Adds a dedicated EjectAction to Disks & Devices that appears in an optical disc's expanded action list while unmounted and hides once mounted (when the default action already ejects). Rightly avoids altering UnmountAction, which only drives the header's unmount-all button. The C++ implementation and CMake wiring are clean, and the UDisks2 mock verification covers both unmounted and mounted optical discs without duplicates.

Correct diagnosis: UnmountAction only feeds the unmount-all header and needs a mounted state, so an inserted but unmounted disc had no eject path; a separate EjectAction in the per-device list, valid only for unmounted optical discs and kept in sync through StateInfo::stateChanged, is the right place and avoids a duplicate Eject once the disc is mounted (where the default action already ejects). It follows the existing ActionInterface/ActionsInfo pattern exactly, and the shots show Mount + Eject on the unmounted disc with Drive.Eject reaching the mock. The check is on Solid::OpticalDisc only, so it should also cover the audio CD from comment 2, though that was not tested. Nit: the OpticalDrive lookup duplicates UnmountAction::triggered() and could be a shared helper.
